pull.title: KAFKA-21240: KRaftMetadataCache should cache metadata request information per image
pull.body:
### What Changed

- Updates `KRaftMetadataRequest` benchmark to more accurately represent
a real scenario by making replica and leader placements random. Also
adds a JBOD case where brokers have >= 1 directory.
- Gets the leader id for a `MetadataResponsePartition` without
constructing a `Node` object.
- `BrokerRegistration`'s in-memory object now maintains a hash set of
online directories so that `BrokerRegistration.hasOnlineDir` no longer
requires a binary search. The previous code is a regression from
ZooKeeper Kafka and can impact performance in JBOD deployments.

### Benchmarking

```
./jmh-benchmarks/jmh.sh -p topicCount=500 -p partitionCount=50 -p
logDirsPerBroker=1,16 -f 10 -prof gc
KRaftMetadataRequestBenchmark.testMetadataRequestForAllTopics
```

```
  ┌──────────────────┬─────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
  │ logDirsPerBroker │  trunk  │   this PR    │    change    │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
  │ 1                │ 2.20 ms │ 1.57–1.65 ms │ −25% to −29% │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
  │ 16               │ 3.52 ms │ 2.50 ms      │ −29%         │
  └──────────────────┴─────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
```

### Alternatives Considered

Storing the `MetadataPartitionResponse` contents directly in-memory via
a LRU cache. Any per-partition state that is being stored by this class
means broker memory usage will scale further with the number of
partitions.

Augmenting the `PartitionRegistration` to contain the fields in the
`MetadataResponse` being computed at request time. I beleive this
approach requires a new MV so that `PartitionRecord` and
`PartitionChangeRecord` can contain the relevant information on disk.
This would mirror ZK the closest in that the controller is responsible
for building the contents of the metadata response, and brokers forwards
it to clients who request metadata.

Both of the above approaches may be "over-kill," so the approach in the
PR is as minimal as possible for now.
